Kabzeel
KAB-zee-el
proper noun
Hebrew Qabts’el, “God gathers” or “whom God gathers,” the southernmost town of Judah.

📖 Biblical Definition

Kabzeel, “God gathers,” was the southernmost of all the towns of Judah, named first in the catalogue of the uttermost cities of the tribe toward the coast of Edom (Jos 15:21). It stood at the very edge of the inheritance, on the dry frontier of the Negeb, where the land of promise gave way to the wilderness and the borders of Edom. Yet this obscure border town was honoured above its fellows as the birthplace of a mighty man: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, “the son of a valiant man, of Kabzeel, who had done many acts” (2Sa 23:20; 1Ch 11:22). Benaiah slew two lionlike men of Moab, went down and slew a lion in the midst of a pit in time of snow, and struck down a great Egyptian with the Egyptian’s own spear; he was set by David over his guard and afterward made captain of the host under Solomon. Thus from the least and farthest town of Judah the LORD raised up one of the foremost of the mighty men. Kabzeel stands as a witness that God gathers His servants from the obscure frontiers of His people, and that the place of one’s birth is no measure of the place to which the LORD may call him; the town whose name confesses that God gathers brought forth a valiant man gathered to the service of the king.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The southernmost town of Judah, birthplace of Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, one of David’s mighty men.

expand to see more

KABZEEL, the southernmost town of Judah (Jos 15:21).

Its name means “God gathers” or “whom God gathers.”

It stood on the dry frontier of the Negeb toward Edom.

It was the birthplace of Benaiah the son of Jehoiada (2Sa 23:20).

Benaiah was a valiant man, captain of David’s guard (1Ch 11:22).

📖 Key Scripture

Jos 15:21 — "And the uttermost cities of the tribe of the children of Judah toward the coast of Edom southward were Kabzeel, and Eder, and Jagur,"

2Sa 23:20 — "And Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, the son of a valiant man, of Kabzeel, who had done many acts, he slew two lionlike men of Moab: he went down also and slew a lion in the midst of a pit in time of snow:"

1Ch 11:22 — "Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, the son of a valiant man of Kabzeel, who had done many acts; he slew two lionlike men of Moab: also he went down and slew a lion in a pit in a snowy day."

Neh 11:25 — "And for the villages, with their fields, some of the children of Judah dwelt at Kirjath-arba, and in the villages thereof, and at Dibon, and in the villages thereof, and at Jekabzeel, and in the villages thereof,"

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A place of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; it witnesses that God gathers His servants from the obscure frontiers of His people.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that God gathers His servants from the obscure frontiers of His people. Kabzeel was the southernmost and least of the towns of Judah, set on the dry edge of the Negeb toward Edom; yet from it the LORD raised up Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, one of the foremost of David’s mighty men. The place of one’s birth is no measure of the place to which God may call him; the town whose name confesses that God gathers brought forth a valiant man gathered to the service of the king.

Benaiah’s deeds — slaying the lionlike men of Moab, going down to kill a lion in a pit in time of snow, striking down the great Egyptian with his own spear — show the strength the LORD gives to those He calls from lowly places. He was set over David’s guard and made captain of Solomon’s host. So the God who gathered him from the far frontier of Kabzeel exalted him to the highest service, a witness that the LORD delights to take the small and obscure and make them mighty for His purposes.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The name means “God gathers” or “whom God gathers,” borne by the southernmost town of Judah.

expand to see more

Kabzeel — Hebrew Qabts’el, “God gathers.”

The element qabats means “to gather.”

The element El means “God.”

It was the southernmost town of Judah, toward Edom.

It was the birthplace of Benaiah the son of Jehoiada.

Usage

"Like Kabzeel, God gathers His servants from the obscure frontiers of His people."

"Kabzeel teaches that the place of one’s birth is no measure of the place God may call him."

"Benaiah of Kabzeel shows that the LORD takes the small and obscure and makes them mighty."
